lastText: File ClosedA Record Argued For, Not AssumedMinor DefeatItalian High Command, 1940 — 1945End of hostilities: MAY 2, 1945Immediate AftermathArmy Group C surrenders in Italy on May 2, 1945, five days ██████ the wider European war ends — the close of nineteen months fighting as a junior Allied partner on Italian soil. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point — Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis █████ relative to ██████████. The delay █████ to buy Rome a coordinated defense instead bought German intelligence two additional days to reinforce the garrison — Operation █████ executed even more completely than its historical version. Rome ███████ Berlin and Madrid for a seat in the Gibraltar question ██████ than settling for Malta or Egypt alone — a diplomatic wager the documented record never records Italy attempting, win or lose at Hendaye's actual table. A deliberate early withdrawal from the Alamein line concedes the same ██████ the historical twelve-day battle ██████████ lost anyway, without first spending the attritional casualties a fuel-starved defense was never ███████ to hold. No branch of this campaign avoids the armistice fork; the war that follows it was already decided by an arithmetic no single command, on either side of the line, could overturn.One Year LaterA year past Army
